authored_description: Table 17-5 calculates the diffraction-limited ground resolution (GSD) of a space imaging system using the relationship GSD = (h x lambda) / D, where h is orbital altitude in km, lambda is the operating wavelength in meters, and D is the aperture diameter in meters. The table provides pre-configured scenarios for three spectral bands — visible (400-750nm), infrared (700nm-300um), and passive microwave (1cm-1m) — at representative orbital altitudes including LEO (~800km), GEO (35,786km), and low-altitude (~15km) orbits. Use this calculation early in concept design to understand the fundamental resolution limit imposed by physics before considering detector, atmosphere, or pointing effects. This is a theoretical ceiling — real system GSD will be worse. For a complete sensor performance estimate including detector pixel size and integration time effects, proceed to Table 17-9.
